generatedProse.concept-context: A reflection is complete only when it produces something you will do differently. In any subject it is easy to reach an insight, such as 'I left the reading too late', and stop there, as if noticing the problem solved it. The stage that makes reflection worth the effort is the one that turns a why into a concrete, usable action: specific enough to carry into the next task, not a general wish to do better.
generatedProse.worked-example:
Consider two students who have both reflected well on why a lab report lost marks.

Student A concludes that the method section was unclear and resolves to write methods more carefully next time. The reflection was sound, but the action is a wish, not a plan. Faced with the next report, Student A has nothing concrete to reach for and slips back into the old habits.

Student B reaches the same insight, then makes it actionable: before writing the next method, they will draft it as a numbered list a classmate could follow, then rewrite it as prose. That is specific, and it can be done. When the next report comes, Student B has an exact first step. The difference is not the quality of the reflection but whether it ended in an action you could actually take.

Both noticed the same problem. Only Student B turned the reflection into a change.
generatedProse.summary: A reflective cycle is finished only when it ends in a concrete action for next time, specific enough to act on rather than a vague intention. You can now tell a usable action from a wish, and turn your own reflections into one small, definite next step. The final lesson brings the three parts together, a structure, critical reflection and a concrete action, as one practice.

check.body: In the worked example, what made Student B's action usable where Student A's was not?

items.text: Student B set a specific, doable next step for the method, not a general intention.
Student B reflected more deeply on why the marks were lost.
Student B felt more strongly about improving.
Student B wrote a longer reflection than Student A.

feedback.correct: Right. A usable action is specific and doable, not a wish to do better.
feedback.incorrectNotFinal: Not quite. Both reflected well; look at whether the action is specific enough to carry out.
feedback.incorrectFinal: Student B's action was usable because it was specific and doable. Deeper feeling, stronger motivation or more words do not make an action actionable.

_prompts.concept-context: What does this look like in practice within the given context? Write a short follow-on from the generic definition above, in the learner's own subject or discipline. Keep it to two or three sentences, mid-register, following straight on from the generic definition.
_prompts.worked-example: Give a subject-specific worked example of this lesson's concept: a weaker or less-developed version first, then a stronger version reached by better practice, using the context cast (character tokens) consistently. Keep the weaker-then-stronger shape and the two-part contrast; name the cast directly in the prose (the pack supplies the whole body). The merge renders it as a block quote, so write it as continuous prose, not as a quoted comment plus commentary.
_prompts.summary: Recap what the learner can now do, in terms of their own subject or context. One short paragraph. Do not restate the learning outcomes verbatim.
_prompts.check: Write the subject's own version of this lesson's check question(s), testing the same outcome in the learner's own discipline. Keep the same number of items and the same correctness pattern as the generic version; reword the stem and items for the subject. Keep the component-level feedback (correct / notFinal / final) teaching, never a bare verdict.
